prompt:
Draw a clean, straight-on CALENDAR PAGE for a month called Nivose, filling most of the frame.

IMPORTANT CALENDAR RULE: in this calendar a week is TEN days long (a 'decade'), NOT seven days. The page must be a grid with exactly TEN day-columns, and the column headings from left to right are: Primidi, Duodi, Tridi, Quartidi, Quintidi, Sextidi, Septidi, Octidi, Nonidi, Decadi. The dates run 1, 2, 3, ... filling the grid left to right and wrapping to a NEW ROW every TEN days (so date 1 is under Primidi, date 10 is under Decadi, date 11 starts the next row under Primidi again, and so on). The month has 30 days.

Draw all 30 dates in the ten-column grid and draw a single red RING around the date 13. Do NOT use a seven-day week and do not add any caption naming the day — the answer is which of the ten day-columns the ringed date 13 falls under.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a CALENDAR PAGE: a grid of dates with named day-columns at the top. Ignoring the number of columns and ignoring artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT a calendar grid (a table of dates with day-name column headings)? A photo, illustration or clean graphic all count as yes. Answer NO only if it is a blank panel, an unrelated object, or just prints a day-name with no grid. Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: This is a calendar grid with named day-columns across the top and a single date circled with a red ring. Look straight UP the column that the red-ringed date sits in and read the day-name HEADING at the top of that same column. Answer with just that one column heading word, exactly as printed.
